arm_kind: same-input review replacement: the premium arm's frozen discovery, study and history artifacts, identical starting state to Arm C. Recall is bounded by what those artifacts contain.
adjudicator: Opus 5 agent (claude-opus-5[1m]); ran no arm; no model-family relationship with the reviewed model

credited.title: Writer authority is stronger than native locks
credited.basis: J0026 L-2e0dc4dec29d states that a per-window worker does not establish repository ownership: the per-window worker thread is documented and implemented (lib.rs:17, gui/mod.rs:918) but 'nothing in the inspected code excludes two workers (two windows, or a window plus the jj CLI) from writing one repository concurrently; consistency is delegated to jj's operation-log merge' (CHANGELOG.md:307, 'Detect changes made by other Jujutsu clients and merge the operation log automatically'). Conclusion stated verbatim: 'per-window workers do not prove a single repository writer.'

credited.title: Exact durable identity and operation-local selectors
credited.basis: The sharpest statement of the operation-local-selector clause in any continuation-4 arm. J0026 separates mutable change id, immutable commit id and the operation-local offset: GG's precise targeting format is change-hex/offset (format_id_str, gui_util.rs:475-480); queries resolve the offset-qualified change symbol and fall back to the known commit id on divergence (gui_util.rs:483-509); mutations accept 'resolved_id == self.wc_id() || resolved_id.hex().starts_with(&id.commit.prefix)' (gui_util.rs:556) - 'commit-prefix comparison plus a current-working-copy exception, not an exact full-id check'; and 'offsets are positional qualifiers resolved as revset symbols against the current operation, nothing immutable is retained across the rewrite'. Verdict: 'an explicit stale-target admission policy, weaker than an exact expected-native-revision rule'.

credited.title: Process failure and cancellation are not no-effect proof
credited.basis: J0021's jj-resolve lead states it from the implementation: cmd_resolve() 'rewrites the commit (rewrite_commit(...).set_tree(new_tree)) and awaits tx.finish() BEFORE checking partial_resolution_error and returning it. A nonzero native outcome therefore does not imply "no native mutation"' (resolve.rs at jj e9f48b3e). J0024 carries the reconciliation half into the Plans: death-before-exit maps to 'effect_unknown/terminal_unknown with after_reconciliation', 'no automatic retry', and the process tree is reaped within the wall timeout, citing Jujutsu_Integration.md:128, :303.

credited.title: Partial multi-file resolve
credited.basis: Verbatim. J0021's jj-resolve lead: 'run_mergetool_external() invokes the tool per conflicted file. An error on the first file returns directly; an error after at least one success breaks the loop and returns the partially resolved tree plus MergeToolPartialResolutionError { source, resolved_count: i }' (external.rs), and 'Abandoning a later file in a custom diffedit3 merge configuration must not be described as rolling back earlier accepted resolutions' (resolve.rs). It then contrasts edit_diff_external, which returns ToolAborted before snapshot_results() so no output snapshot occurs.

credited.title: Native versus sidecar crash boundary
credited.basis: J0023 item 8 states both halves. Independent observability across partial failure: the manifest file is published atomically (tmp+rename, mirror_manifest.rs:264-283) but 'the mirror tree itself has no transactional publication' - TUS finalize renames one file at a time, normalize edits markers in place, and the client pull 'writes straight into the live local repo with std::fs::write ... no staging area, no isolated disposable validation before activation'. Do-not-trust-a-healthy-looking-graph: J0020 and J0028 establish that refs can agree via ls-remote while the object store is torn, catchable only by a full fsck, and J0020 records that sync runs git_store_needs_healing as a pre-flight before letting jj op log read.

credited.title: Hunk and editable diff safety
credited.basis: J0022's proposal item 1-2 binds editable saves to both sides, native conflict state and exact identity: a typed per-file save entry 'plus backend conflict_id and expected snapshot/operation identity per file', and 'Save validation bound to session/repository/snapshot identity (per JJI-002), never path membership alone'. The owning requirement is quoted - JJI-005 'Conflict resolution proves current snapshot, expected conflict identity, and terminal reconciliation' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:199) - against diffedit3's membership-only validator (types.rs:80-105), 'the anti-pattern JJI-002 forbids'.

credited.title: Empty, absent and failed reads are distinct
credited.basis: Three distinct instances of the proposition. (1) Missing content becomes a valid empty file: 'to_text() returns null for non-Text ... widget config uses to_text(input.edit) ?? "" ... save_unchecked only create_dir_all(parent) + std::fs::write - no deletion operation' (backend_interactions.ts:11-16, merge_state.ts:239-242, fs.rs:24-52), with README listing the written-empty-file as a known bug. (2) Traversal omission: 'filter_map(|e| e.ok()) drops traversal errors' and non-regular entries are skipped so type collisions read as Missing (fs.rs:103-133). (3) A failed native query becomes an empty list: J0026 concern 1 - get_page's 'while let Some(Ok(...))' terminates on a RevsetEvaluationError with no error path, so 'a mid-query revset evaluation error is therefore presented as (possibly premature) end-of-history' (queries.rs:161).

credited.title: Diff text and metadata round-trip
credited.basis:
All three clauses. Untouched bytes and line endings: the chain is traced end to end at the pin - values() exports every editor including untouched ones (merge_state.ts:37-44), no lineSeparator key exists anywhere, package-lock pins codemirror 5.65.20, and CodeMirror splitLinesAuto / lineSep||'
' (Doc.js:418-422) yields 'an untouched a
b
 becomes a
b
 after Save; mixed endings collapse to LF', with jj's diff_working_copies.rs setting EolConversionMode::None so workspace EOL config cannot restore the bytes. Deletion state: 'Missing becomes "" in the UI and a written empty file on save'. Metadata: FileEntry carries '// TODO: Track executable bit, other metadata perhaps' (types.rs:5-13), and J0021 adds the precise limit - 'fs::write never chmods, so existing-file truncation retains the existing mode ... existing executable bits are not established to be lost by a save'.

credited.title: External editor path confinement
credited.basis: The full counterexample chain, source-verified. J0021's symlink-write lead: left/x regular, right/x and output/x symlinks outside the tree; scan() filters to regular files so x renders as an editable empty middle pane; 'the allowlist is the union of scanned input paths ... It validates the name only - not output type, canonical target, or an open handle - and is recomputed per save, not a fixed snapshot' (types.rs); 'Save calls std::fs::write(output.join("x"), contents) ... no O_NOFOLLOW in this path. The symlink's referent is truncated/written'. It then shows the layout arises naturally because jj materializes real symlinks into the output tree, and contrasts jj's own checkout, which uses create_new(true) 'Don't overwrite, don't follow symlink' (local_working_copy.rs:786/2080) - 'protection diffedit3's save path does not share'. Ancestor and root cases are named: output-ancestor directory symlinks and WalkDir's follow_root_links default.

credited.title: Partial external editor writes
credited.basis: Verbatim, and it separates the two outcomes upstream. 'Validation rejection prevents all writes; mid-save I/O failure does not roll back': dirs_save/single_file_save submit an invalid key first and 'the post-state snapshot is unchanged' (fs.rs:259-275, 337-356), while files_and_dirs_mix_save_error 'writes file successfully, then fails writing the output root, with TODO "make sure nothing is changed by the failed save" - a concrete source-level partial-write path' (fs.rs:378-421). J0022's proposal item 4 supplies the PM answer: stage-then-commit or journaled rollback per the forge_backup acceptance pattern, with partial failure exposing the old state and a typed recovery boundary.

credited.title: External diff and merge tool handoff
credited.basis: J0024's proposal is the managed session in full, including the remote-forwarding clause. It requires 'a tool readiness signal distinct from process spawn/browser open (an authenticated GET of merge data fetched by PM, per CV-307's do not mark a surface ready from configuration presence alone)'; an ObservableWork session record bound to exact Execution Host/Environment/Source Location; terminal outcome 'receipt-backed only'; and 'wall timeout plus process-tree cancellation on the tool process'. Remote: jj ships diffedit3 and diffedit3-ssh profiles (merge_tools.toml; docs/config.md:974-1003 at jj e6dd2c0d), and the arm records that SSH stdio does not fit diffedit3's HTTP API so forwarding is the only documented remote mode, with LSPSupport.md:584-605 as the contrasting precedent. Acceptance checks 1-6 track readiness, save, exit, kill/cleanup and remote binding separately.

credited.title: External editor stale sessions
credited.basis: The proposition including its identical-filenames clause. J0022 records that the validator 'rescans and checks path membership only (types.rs:80-105)' and 'binds neither contents nor repository/snapshot/session identity', with the upstream comment naming a frontend 'connected to a different server'. The proposal's item 2 and its acceptance check state the obligation: 'stale or reconnected-server payloads are rejected before any write' and 'stale-identity payload (same paths, different server/snapshot) rejected before any write'.

credited.title: Bound reads before allocating
credited.basis: Stated with the upstream TODO as evidence: 'MAX_FILE_LENGTH: usize = 200_000 ... read_to_string completes before the contents.len() > MAX_FILE_LENGTH and NUL checks (TODOs: "read no more than MAX_FILE_LENGTH")' (fs.rs:101, 103-133). The preserved-partial-and-error-states half is the same passage's 'filter_map(|e| e.ok()) drops traversal errors'. J0022 carries it into the proposal as 'bounded reads (size checked before allocation)'. The arm also corrects the prose bound: 'Code: 200_000 bytes ... Prose: CHANGELOG.md:130 "over 200KiB" ... 200 KiB = 204,800; use the code bound.'

credited.title: Authenticated browser and local IPC
credited.basis: J0024 states all three clauses against the owning fixtures. Authentication: 'diffedit3 binds 127.0.0.1 and has no token/origin/session check in its app routes; admission is only a per-save relative-path allowlist', and 'PM would need its own session secret + host binding in front of it'. Caller/repository binding: the corpus's negative fixture is quoted - negative.web_client_loopback_assumption (remote_access_system_contract_fixtures.json:4143-4168) with web_client_loopback_assumed as an explicit false-required schema field, plus 'A localhost redirect on the laptop is not the container's localhost' (forge_backup_tsnet_acceptance.json:1007). Stale instances: acceptance check 6 requires that 'a forwarded loopback URL from a different client/session is rejected'.

credited.title: Included tools and exact qualification
credited.basis: Stated on both sides of the version question. PM side: 'Jujutsu 0.44.0 is retained only as an initial packet certification input pending current official re-verification' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:331) and unsupported versions 'degrade reads and fail mutations closed' (:233); J0024 adds JJI-006's requirement that setup 'reports requested and effective capabilities separately' and that absence of a tool yields 'a typed disabled reason, never a launch attempt'. External side: Dojjo pins jj-lib 0.38.0 in two crates with the documented instruction to 're-audit dojjo-mirror/src/mirror_exclude.rs FileLock paths against the new tree' on a bump, and the arm states 'Parity with the brief's 0.44.0 profile must not be assumed; the pin is real.'

credited.title: Colocated import/export stays fail-closed
credited.basis: Quoted to the exact fixture and disabled reason: colocated import/export 'stays effective-false without the exact adapter and live environment having current certification evidence' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:224-225), fixture jj_0_44_colocated_import_export_defaults_false_without_fallback (source_control_contract_fixtures.json:244) and disabled reason jj_0_44_colocated_import_export_disabled_upstream_race (source_control_contracts.schema.json:964). J0028 uses it to refuse a version-parity assumption rather than to describe a feature.

credited.title: Windows links and native file types
credited.basis: The dedicated extracted lead is the proposition. 'Interactive split of a commit containing an added symlink: the first change receives a regular file whose content is the symlink target; the symlink materializes only in the remaining change'; 'jj commit -i ... selected symlink rows produce mode 100644 instead of 120000 even with both content and file-mode rows selected'; and the transfer statement: 'Preserve symbolic link identity separately from link target text and from target-file contents in any diff/selection model', then 'test dangling, ignored-target, unchanged-target, changed-target, and type-only transitions independently'. Receipts are jj #8671 (S00027/S00038), #9210 (S00058), #9211 (S00055), with the arm refusing to assume one root cause. The Windows half is named as deferred, not claimed.

credited.title: Native conflict truth and supported shape
credited.basis: J0022 states it and keeps the boundary. The owning text is quoted - JJI-005 'Conflicts remain typed JJ conflicts with materialized-file and backend state explicitly distinguished' (:191) and 'Do not call a materialized file clean while JJ conflict state remains' (:208) - and the arm states its own limit explicitly: 'none of this is a recommendation to substitute file text for native conflict state'. The proposal's typed entry carries backend conflict_id alongside the file state so that 'the empty-vs-deleted conflation is structurally impossible', and its acceptance checks require distinct outcomes for missing versus text("").

credited.title: Push targets and bookmark effects
credited.basis: J0023's L-444f31e68545 preserves the axes and demands exact effect scope. Axes, with a correction to the handoff: 'tracked and synced are two independent axes of a remote bookmark (a ref can be tracked-but-unsynced); "absent" describes the remote bookmark whose local counterpart ref is gone' (DESIGN.md:42-47), code-confirmed at RevisionObject.svelte:75/109. Exact effects: the full action-scope table - 'Untrack → tracking/combined chip untracks all remotes, unsynced remote chip untracks one ... Rename → tracking/combined untracks first ... Delete → local/combined deletes the local ref, remote chip forgets the remote ref (also clearing pending deletes)' - with the stated obligation 'confirmations/labels must name the scope (all remotes vs one; local ref vs remote ref; rename-after-untrack side effect)'. The 0.35.2 pseudo-remote 'git' push-target defect is cited as the concrete failure.

credited.title: Graph bounds, continuity and isolation
credited.basis: The strongest continuation-4 statement of the continuity clause, made from source rather than from a contract. Binding to identity: 'page continuation is bound only to the revset string. QueryLogNextPage re-resolves self.session.latest_query (session.rs:309-310) and handle_query re-evaluates the revset against the current repo state (session.rs:524-538); no operation identity, revset snapshot, or config identity is retained. So a mutation between pages (from any writer) can silently change what the next page streams - this makes "bind continuation to operation/revset/config identity" and "ensure no lost/duplicated commit across interruption" concrete, observed gaps rather than speculative advice.' Missing/partial edges: LogLine::ToMissing and indirect flags (queries.rs:239-298). Page bounds: visual rows increment row before the boundary check (queries.rs:297-300). Resume: the skip loop 'over-consumes by the number of previously counted visual rows; those commits are silently never rendered'.

credited.title: Graph visual and menu regressions
credited.basis: J0023 item 5 verifies each regression at the pinned revision and states the checklist: 0.38.4 'Dragging a revision onto a parent edge no longer drops other parents when the rebased child is a merge commit'; 0.38.0 web-mode right-click 'enabled commands from the selected revision rather than the clicked one'; 0.37.1 'revision-menu commands applied to every open window'; 0.35.2 graph-render rework unbreaking bookmark drag-drop; 0.38.4 drop-target fix for vertical segments of curved graph lines. Conclusion: 'the risk concentrates in (a) drop-target resolution vs rendered graph geometry, (b) context/menu scoping to the clicked vs selected operand, (c) per-window command routing - a concrete checklist for any equivalent surface.'

credited.title: Direct graph manipulation
credited.basis: J0023's L-0793ad1e2a78 covers the gestures and the preconditions, code-verified. Gestures: drag to rebase, into/out of parents to add merges or move subtrees, or abandon; drag files to squash or restore; drag bookmarks; double-click resolved in code to create_revision when immutable and checkout_revision otherwise (RevisionMutator.ts:86-101). Multi-selection: range select with combined change/conflict view and range drag-drop, with the spec's load-bearing constraints the handoff missed - 'selection is linear-only (single-parent, contiguous, no elided commits)', range drag-drop uses MoveRevisions/InsertRevisions/AdoptRevision, and 'Edit/Describe/Restore are disabled for ranges as semantically ambiguous'. The remaining obligations are named explicitly: 'Slint equivalents - target previews, keyboard/context-menu parity - and tracing which native jj commands each worker mutation invokes'.

credited.title: Description drafts survive refresh
credited.basis: J0026 verifies the behaviour and its identity key: GG 0.41.0 'Draft descriptions are saved across operations as long as the change-id of your selection remains the same' (CHANGELOG.md:14), confirmed with the stated nuance that 'preservation is keyed on the selection's change-id'. It is placed inside the same lead's finding that a change-id is not a sufficient identity - offsets are positional and nothing immutable is retained across a rewrite - so draft survival is tied to exact identity rather than to a refresh.

credited.title: Immutable content caches and async selection
credited.basis: Two of the three clauses explicitly, with citations. Immutable keys versus mutable generations: 'offsets are positional qualifiers resolved as revset symbols against the current operation (gui_util.rs:484-485, 541-542); nothing immutable is retained across the rewrite', and the lead's rule 'Raw offsets may shift as history changes; bind immutable IDs' is marked a sound inference from the verified mechanism. Never present degraded data as complete: concern 1 - a mid-query RevsetEvaluationError is delivered as end-of-history with has_more computed from a re-poll 'that can consume a second error as end-of-stream'. The late-response clause is the weakest: the arm records that 'there is no explicit cancel API ... Invalidation is implicit (event-driven), not policy-driven' rather than requiring quarantine.

credited.title: One catalog and authoritative eligibility
credited.basis: J0024 and J0028 state all three clauses with owner citations. One catalog: 'every cmd.jujutsu.* row is handler_unavailable; owner result/receipt/projection only' (Commands_System.md:5527), consumers may not 'issue direct jj subprocesses outside the adapter' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:36), and the command_id enum 'is exactly 31 commands' (jujutsu_integration_contracts.schema.json:86-118). Idempotent command instances: 'idempotent command instance required per mutation' (Source_Control_System.md:129). Exact work attribution: 'ObservableWork is the single shared truth for phase, wait reason, progress, cancellation, and terminal outcome. A spinner, command dispatch receipt, or connection state is not work truth' (Shared_Integration_Runtime.md:39).

credited.title: Runtime evidence versus unused scaffolding
credited.basis: The best external instance of this proposition in the experiment: a documented capability that no consumer implements. J0020 correction 1 - 'Push/fetch need is telemetry-only today. git_transport_need's doc comment promises "When both are false, skip git push / git fetch so idle sync does not rewrite mirrored paths", but the only consumer (client/src/sync.rs line ~73) records git_skipped in sync-debug records; git_push_dojjo and git_fetch_dojjo run unconditionally every dev sync round. No other caller gates on it (checked client/src/background_sync.rs, mirror_pull.rs - no usage).' Correction 2 adds that even if it were wired up 'it could never trigger on a machine that has ever fetched'. J0024 supplies the PM-side rule: a nominal flag is not readiness - 'do not mark a surface ready from configuration presence alone' (CV-307) - and records that 'merge_editor_available is not defined by any owner in the corpus (single occurrence)'.

credited.title: Process execution follows owner environment
credited.basis: J0024 states the owner-environment rule and the fence set: consumers may not 'issue direct jj subprocesses outside the adapter' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:36), 'Direct UI-to-process jj execution ... and fallback Git mutation are forbidden' (:333, quoted in J0028); the external tool must run under 'Shared_Integration_Runtime process governance (bounded external-process pools, line 837)', 'wall timeout plus process-tree cancellation', 'BinaryLocator-style deterministic tool discovery if the tool is located rather than configured', and Permissions plus FileSafe admission of its file writes. The plugin-contract fence set is quoted by field: network_access (none|loopback_declared|https_allowlisted), off_loopback_transport, wall_timeout_ms, process_tree_cancellation, stdout_max_bytes/stderr_max_bytes, symlink_policy. J0020's external evidence is the matching hygiene: git_command() removes GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE.

credited.title: Complete retained native backup closure
credited.basis: JJI-008's closure text is quoted in full and used as the governing answer: closure must include 'operation heads/store, referenced views, commits/trees/conflicts, non-current abandoned/rebased objects ... underlying Git/common/alternate/shared stores when present, workspace maps and captured dirty files' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:449-452) under 'one capture barrier and GC/prune/rewrite fence' (:452-453), and 'a text op log, Git push, mirror clone, Git bundle, current bookmarks, or remote availability alone cannot satisfy it' (:466). The arm supplies the external demonstration: J0023 states that Dojjo's replication path has 'no GC fencing, no dirty-file capture, no isolation before activation anywhere', and J0026 adds that jj's operation/view/extra metadata 'lives in the separate extra/ TableStore inside the jj store, outside the Git object store - confirming git fsck alone does not validate native operation/view/extra metadata closure.'

credited.title: Snapshot omission and skipped checkout
credited.basis: J0028 states the distinction as an owned requirement with its citation: 'Capture cannot manufacture a JJ snapshot/commit/operation to align dirty files with the last recorded operation; the closure and restore receipt disclose the captured-files relationship separately' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:467), with fixture backup_jj_colocated_closure_captures_git_common_store_and_dirty_files (jujutsu_integration_contract_fixtures.json:2782) and BRS-017's rule that an offline required source 'waits or yields explicit partial status'. The unsupported-content half is established externally by J0021: NUL, invalid UTF-8 and files over 200,000 bytes are Unsupported and symlinks and directories scan as missing, so an editor's view of a tree is not the tree.

credited.title: Backup existence is not verified recovery
credited.basis: The arm's own concrete repair is this proposition made discriminating. J0028: JJI-008 requires restore verification to 'restore the selected historical operation with object verification' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:468) but 'No Plan, schema, or fixture defines what object verification must detect', and the proposed replacement is 'full object-store integrity verification - commits, trees, and blob contents are read and checked (Git fsck default-class semantics); a connectivity-only check cannot satisfy this, and agreement of refs, bookmarks, or operation-log text alone cannot pass verification.' Its acceptance checks are a torn-pack negative, a byte-flipped-blob negative ('the discriminating test'), a positive on the disposable copy, and all three across colocated, non-colocated and shared layouts. The isolation clause is quoted too: verification runs on 'a clean isolated disposable repository' and never on the original (:453-455, :501).

credited.title: Extras head integrity and crash corruption
credited.basis: J0020 verifies the extras-head mechanism and its integrity question at the source: normalize_extra_table_heads 'loads TableStore from mirror/store/extra, calls get_head(), and persist_extra_table_head_marker re-writes the empty marker file store/extra/heads/<segment-id> (128-char hex segment name asserted)', because 'get_head_locked() can merge divergent markers yet leave no marker files on disk ... we restore the pointer after JJ picks the canonical segment id'; the upstream fix is located precisely as jj PR #9648 fixing issue #9649, merged 2026-08-28, against Dojjo's jj-lib 0.38.0 pin. The keep-ref half: fsck is run 'to catch "torn pack, or refs/jj/keep/* pointing at missing commits"', and the retention question is left open rather than asserted - 'no code path in dojjo runs git gc ... Not established either way.' The do-not-call-everything-corruption clause is J0028's separation of a missing-object closure receipt from a corrupt-blob failure.

credited.title: Sanitized inactive restore configuration
credited.basis: Stated with its citations: restored credentials and config are sanitized-inactive and 'require the credential/profile owner to revalidate ... and a fresh operation lease before use' (Source_Control_System.md:797-798; Jujutsu_Integration.md:456, :471). The external counterpart is J0020's verified exclusion set - config.toml, config-id, store/git_target and workspace_store are local-only and never mirrored - and its recorded weakness, that Dojjo's create progress carries 'stale api_base/git_remote_url ... only partially re-fetched when empty'.

credited.title: Capture generation differs from upload resume
credited.basis: J0020 states the proposition against a real resumable setup. Verified: phases ServerRegistered -> Rehomed -> GitPushed are persisted and skipped on retry, and mirror uploads are skipped only when the manifest entry's sha256 AND size match, 'with a post-upload verification pass (size+sha256 re-read) before state is saved'. The gap is stated as the requirement: 'Durable phase receipts with evidence before replay: the GitPushed phase marker records that push was attempted/completed but carries no server-side evidence; replay relies on push idempotence rather than a receipt', plus 'config revalidation on resume (stale api_base/git_remote_url in progress are only partially re-fetched when empty)'. J0028 names the owning rule: 'Move/resume checkpoints carry the exact operation and workspace reconstruction evidence' (Jujutsu_Integration.md:92).

credited.title: Clone completion and cleanup
credited.basis: J0020 tracks the multi-stage setup and its destination protection at the source: create re-homes .jj/repo and leaves a pointer file, with each phase persisted and 'infer_create_progress' reconstructing the phase when the crash preceded the progress file; 'Join requires empty destination: prepare_workspace_root bails if .jj exists or any entry other than .dojjo is present' and 'assert_cwd_not_jj_workspace refuses to run inside any JJ workspace'; cold versus warm join is decided by is_local_dojo_join_ready. The residual-state clause is recorded as the open case: 'a stale .dojjo entry is the one allowed pre-existing file - interaction with a prior failed join is untested'. J0028 supplies the identity rule that must replace the name check: 'one conflict plan compares exact resource identities ... paths, focus, labels, and repository proximity never substitute for resource identity' (Source_Control_System.md:428-431).

credited.title: Parent retention in history edits
credited.basis: J0023 states it from the changelog and the implementation. The defect: 0.38.4 'Dragging a revision onto a parent edge no longer drops other parents when the rebased child is a merge commit' (CHANGELOG line 71), verified at the pin. The descendant half: the 0.36 hunk algorithm is code-verified as 'Split-rebase-squash' in MoveHunk::execute - 'source rewritten + descendants rebased (jj rebase analogue), destination receives the hunk via 3-way merge ... with distinct child->parent / parent->child / unrelated ancestry strategies' (change.rs:267-442) - and the arm records that 'hunk moves refuse merge-commit sources (lines 277-279)' rather than approximating them.

credited.title: Performance mechanisms are not capability proof
credited.basis: Bounds honesty made concrete and checkable. J0026 concern 2: a missing-edge visual row 'adds no LogRow but increments row (queries.rs:297) before the boundary check row == max (queries.rs:300). A page can deliver page_size - 1 commit rows plus one visual row, and next_row accounting includes visual rows.' Concern 3 turns the same accounting error into data loss on resume: QuerySession::new skips state.next_row stream items where one stream item is one commit, but next_row counted commit rows plus virtual rows, so 'the skip loop over-consumes ... those commits are silently never rendered while stems/graph lines stay self-consistent'. The arm states the standard it is holding the design to - the lookahead pagination is 'a usable comparator ... with three specific boundary behaviors to avoid or handle explicitly' - and refuses an unsupported performance inference elsewhere: a GitHub search returning total_count 0 'does not establish absence of reports'.

credited.title: Upstream narrative inconsistencies
credited.basis: Sustained across every job, and it is this arm's signature. J0017: the handoff's 'fs.rs L424' citation is wrong for the pinned revision ('the loop is fs.rs:24-52; line 424 is deleted_lhs_file'); the frontend comment claiming the server guesses empty-versus-missing 'is stale - the server does not guess; guessing exists only as the backend TODO'; and the prose bound '200KiB' is refuted by the code bound 200_000. J0020: Dojjo's own comment 'Do not use --connectivity-only: it skips unreachable refs such as refs/jj/keep/*' is refuted from git-fsck(1) - both modes use the refs namespace as heads; what --connectivity-only actually skips is blob reading - so 'the practice (full fsck) remains justified ... but the comments attribute it to the wrong mechanism'; and the header comment claiming the entire Git repository moves by fetch/push is corrected ('client config is never transported; client HEAD is realigned locally by git checkout -B'). J0023: three parent-prose corrections, including that mirror_apply_order computes rather than writes, and cycles are caught in the toposort rather than in operation_expand. J0026: 'Correction: common_dir is not jj code at v0.44.0 ... commondir handling is gix's, consumed implicitly', which changes how a closure manifest must be derived.

partial_matches.title: Terminal attempts always have receipts
partial_matches.why_partial: J0028 quotes the existing requirement - 'every terminal attempt emits a typed operation receipt even when the effect is unknown or recovery is required' (Source_Control_System.md:130-131) - and J0024 lists the seven typed results including effect_unknown. Neither states the correction: that a contract shape permits a terminal attempt with a null receipt. The arm treats the obligation as satisfied rather than finding where it is not enforced.

partial_matches.title: Expected operation is not native compare-and-swap
partial_matches.why_partial: J0026 gets the strongest half - GG's admission is 'an explicit stale-target admission policy, weaker than an exact expected-native-revision rule' (gui_util.rs:537-571) - and J0028 quotes 'Every JJ mutation compares the expected operation and immutable commit identity'. What is missing is the distinguishing clause: nothing in the corpus says --at-operation selects a starting view rather than performing a compare-and-swap, or addresses the after-a-long-fetch case. Credited as F006, which is what the arm actually proves.

partial_matches.title: Unknown auth retry effects
partial_matches.why_partial: J0024 and J0028 assert the general rule ('Do not retry an effect-unknown mutation automatically', Source_Control_System.md:154) and apply it to a killed editor process. The credential-specific proposition - do not copy fail-prompt-retry credential flows unless the prior operation is proven safe to replay under the same command instance - is not stated; no credential retry flow is examined.

partial_matches.title: Edited text line-ending policy
partial_matches.why_partial: The preservation clause is asserted twice ('untouched CRLF file byte-identical after save'; 'Unchanged files byte-identical on save (no re-encode; line endings preserved per the FileManager.md:349 principle)'), but the product choice itself - which newline convention applies to genuinely newly inserted or replaced boundaries in mixed-ending edited text - is never posed. J0021 asks only whether a no-edit Save can round-trip and whether unsupported combinations should disable saving. muse13 and claude-hicap were credited because each poses the edited-row policy explicitly; this arm does not.

partial_matches.title: Credential architecture and custody already chosen
partial_matches.why_partial: J0024 asserts authenticated IPC, operation/session binding, typed waits ('browser-open failure alone is non-fatal and surfaces as a typed wait reason') and the loopback-is-not-authorization negative. It does not reach the credential half of the proposition: the owner-brokered HTTPS/SSH paths, operation-scoped credential leases and the refusal to copy a raw askpass architecture are not discussed, because no credential flow was in this arm's leads.

partial_matches.title: Git HEAD and index health are separate
partial_matches.why_partial: J0026 proves the structural half from gitrepository-layout: HEAD (298-312) and index (346-348) carry no $GIT_COMMON_DIR redirection clause and are therefore workspace-sensitive, split indexes use sharedindex.<SHA-1> 'only valid in split index mode', and refs/bisect, refs/rewritten, refs/worktree and logs/HEAD stay per-worktree. J0020 adds that a client's Git HEAD is realigned locally by git checkout -B rather than transported. What is not asserted is the finding's actual point: that colocated Git HEAD, index entries and index recovery state must be qualified separately from JJ status.

partial_matches.title: Read preview and dry-run side effects
partial_matches.why_partial: J0024 gets close - 'a no-edit save can change the tree jj snapshots ... users would see spurious diffs' - which is a read-shaped action with real effects. But the proposition is about preview, dry-run and immutable-override retry being labelled read-only by a client; none of those three is examined.

partial_matches.title: Partial clone and LFS/submodule eligibility
partial_matches.why_partial: J0026 establishes the non-self-contained store set from primary sources - shallow clones and alternates including $GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES (gitrepository-layout 226-234), jj v0.44.0's shallow_root_ids cached from gix shallow_commits() with shallow commits treated as parentless and a TODO on unshallow consistency (git_backend.rs:371-380) - and states 'Shallow/partial data is therefore a supported adapter state that a closure drill must detect, not a hypothetical'. That is the shallow half. Partial/promisor, LFS and nested/submodule qualification, and the never-silently-hydrate clause, are not stated.

partial_matches.title: Operation metadata is not idempotency
partial_matches.why_partial: J0028 asserts that a durable command instance is required per mutation and that Dojjo's GitPushed phase marker 'carries no server-side evidence and resume replays on assumed push idempotence'. That is a progress marker, not the finding's subject: native operation descriptions and rewritten operation IDs being treated as a substitute for durable command-instance identity. Credited as F085, which is what the arm actually proves.

partial_matches.title: Graph page consistency and adjacency bounds
partial_matches.why_partial: THE ARM HAD THE EVIDENCE AND NEVER ROUTED IT. J0026's three confirmed GG defects are the external form of three of F107's four clauses - emitted counts versus page bounds (visual rows counted against the boundary), usable continuation on a page claiming more data (continuation bound only to the revset string; the resume skip silently drops commits), and unambiguous node identity (change-id offset plus commit prefix plus a working-copy exception). But J0026 was a reconcile job under an external-only assignment, and no compare job in this arm took a graph lead, so the defect was never stated against the SourceGraph contract. F061 and F092 capture what the arm did deliver.
